sources.entry: pypandoc - A thin wrapper for pandoc, the universal document converter.

summary.one_liner: pypandoc is a thin Python wrapper around the pandoc universal document converter, for converting files and strings between markup formats from Python code or the command line.
summary.what_it_does: Provides convert_file and convert_text functions that call the pandoc binary and return the converted output as a Unicode string, or write directly to an output file. Accepts single files, glob patterns, lists of inputs, and pathlib paths. Supports passing pandoc command-line options through extra_args, pandoc filters (including Lua filters) through filters, and format overrides. Can download a pandoc binary (download_pandoc or the pypandoc download CLI) and includes helpers to report the pandoc version, binary path, and supported formats. With the optional tinytex extra, it integrates with pytinytex to install a TinyTeX LaTeX distribution and automatically install missing LaTeX packages when converting to PDF or LaTeX.
use_cases: convert Markdown files to Word docx
generate PDF from Markdown with pandoc
convert between reStructuredText, HTML and Markdown in Python
batch convert a folder of documents
apply pandoc filters during document conversion
notable: Two installs: pypandoc uses a system pandoc, while pypandoc_binary bundles pandoc
Automatic retry that installs missing LaTeX packages via tlmgr when PDF conversion fails
Built-in CLI that passes arguments straight through to the pandoc binary
Accepts glob patterns, lists, and pathlib objects as inputs
caveats: Requires a pandoc installation: either installed separately or via the pypandoc_binary package
The bundled pandoc binary is only downloaded for Windows, Mac OS X, and 64-bit Intel Linux builds
Converting to PDF or LaTeX needs a LaTeX engine, supplied by TinyTeX via the tinytex extra or installed manually
Some formats (such as docx, epub, pdf) can only be written to a file via outputfile
